title: State-space address memory for Mirror codes
hypothesis: A two-coordinate Mirror address stored in recurrent SSM state recalls a selected logical transition after 512 distractor steps at <=1.10x external-register NRMSE, <=60% external-state bytes, <=1.25x MAC, and <=10% drift growth from delay 8.
mirror_coordinate: two-coordinate dynamically written and retained address m
logical_multiplicity: four selected transition functions recalled after distractors

task.teacher: cue selects one of four stable transitions; distractors intervene; query asks for selected transition response

storage.authority: actual serialized inference payload and recurrent-state bytes
paid_objects: external address or recurrent m/register state

success_gate: Every fresh world at delay 512: Mirror recall NRMSE <=1.10x external; Mirror state bytes <=60% external; MAC <=1.25x; normalized error drift from delay 8 <=10%.
failure_gate: Any registered quality/byte/compute/drift gate fails or equal-width ordinary register/fast-weight control matches at lower bytes.
boundaries: No natural SSM or language-model retention claim.
State bytes include all persistent address memory.

amendments.reason: Initial development/fresh audit found initialized retention alpha=sigmoid(-4)=0.018, so the address decayed before distractors and non-external recall stayed at chance. Correct to a near-persistent alpha initialization sigmoid(6)=0.9975. No metric, gate, data world, or update count changes. Initial fresh rows are invalidated and will be overwritten after rerun.

Post-run audit found runner used recall NLL for development selection and primary results while frozen contract specified recall NRMSE. Change metric to probability-vector NRMSE against one-hot target, retain accuracy and NLL as secondary diagnostics, and rerun development/fresh on same splits. No gate or world/seed changes.
